stem: A random variable X takes values 1, 2, 3 and 4 with probabilities 0.1, 0.3, 0.4 and 0.2 respectively. What is E(X)?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Averaging values 1+2+3+4 divided by 4 gives 2.5, ignoring the probability weights entirely.
Using unweighted sum of values divided by 2 (midpoint of range) yields 3.0.
Using only value multiplied by the first probability 0.1 scaled by 20 produces 2.0, misreading the distribution.

explanation: Expected value is the probability-weighted average of all values. Multiply each value by its probability and sum: 1x0.1 + 2x0.3 + 3x0.4 + 4x0.2 = 0.1 + 0.6 + 1.2 + 0.8 = 2.7.

explanation_sections.punchline: E(X) is the weighted sum of all values using probabilities as weights, not a simple average of the values.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: discrete random variable with given probability mass function. Map each (x, p) pair, compute x*p for each, then sum. Here: 0.1 + 0.6 + 1.2 + 0.8 = 2.7.
explanation_sections.lesson: E(X) = sum of (value times probability) over all outcomes; never divide by n unless all probabilities are equal.
explanation_sections.timing: 45 seconds. Write out 4 products mentally and add. The trap is using the simple mean 2.5 instead of the weighted mean.
